text.en: Look up: sun, clouds, a breeze. The air around the Earth is a thin but vital blanket. It gives us oxygen, controls temperature and brings the monsoon rains.

The atmosphere is made mainly of nitrogen, about 78 percent, and oxygen, about 21 percent, with small amounts of argon, carbon dioxide and water vapour.
It has layers: troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere and exosphere. Weather happens in the troposphere.
The ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays from the Sun.
Weather is the day-to-day state of the atmosphere; climate is its average over a long time.
Temperature, pressure, winds, humidity and rainfall are the elements of weather and climate.
The monsoon is a seasonal reversal of winds. In summer, moist winds from the sea blow towards heated land and bring rain.
Burning fuels adds carbon dioxide and raises the carbon footprint, the total greenhouse gases we cause.
We can reduce it by saving energy, using public transport, planting trees and avoiding waste.

problem.en: Why does the monsoon bring rain to India in summer?

text.en: Land heats faster than the sea, so air over land rises.
Moist air from the ocean rushes in.
It rises, cools and falls as rain.

prompt.en: Differentiate weather from climate and name the layers of the atmosphere.

commonMisconceptions.en: Using the words as the same thing

points.en: The air is mostly nitrogen and oxygen.
Weather is short-term; climate is long-term.
Monsoon winds reverse with the season.
We can reduce our carbon footprint.
